Tests call gates through ddflow, no full-suite run.

ddflow/services/metrics/tiny.py new 'tiny' view (tiny-cold counts, per-gate seconds, confirmed HIGH/MEDIUM finding rate from review.triaged, later-bug rate by size bucket; file-count limits/same-file-refix/bundle-savings named not_measured), review.triaged fold in facts.py, [fasttrack] section + 5 knob fragments under templates/upgrade/unreleased, 'tiny' wired into service.py. chunk_findings.detail: Items whose size was never recorded are treated as failing the tiny-cold line limit. `_size_of` returns 0 when every outcome has `changed_lines` missing, and `_size_bucket` says that 0 “says nothing”, but `_tiny_cold` still puts those spans in `total` and only increments `count` when `0 < lines <= tiny_cold_max_source_lines`. Two completed items with no `changed_lines` therefore become `count=0`, `total=2` and, once `min_samples` is met, a 0% rate: “0 of 2 completed items met the source-line limit”. They were not measured, so that zero is a false fail [r-unavailable-not-pass]. The same mix (one 5-line item and one unmeasured item) is reported as 50% instead of 1 of 1 measured.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/tiny.py:_tiny_cold

chunk_findings.detail: `bundle_savings` is listed under `not_measured`, but the shipped reason states “the saved gate-seconds are zero until the first bundle lands”. That asserts a numeric zero the log does not support. Intent is unavailable-not-zero, and bundling having never been observed is not evidence that savings were zero.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/tiny.py:NOT_MEASURED

chunk_findings.detail: A missing completion time is coerced to epoch. `at > (s.completed_at or 0)` treats `completed_at` of `None` or `0` as time 0, so any bug timestamp `> 0` on that item is a “later” bug. A completed span with no `completed_at` and a bug filed at t=1 is counted in `later` and raises `later_bug_rate` even though the bug is not known to be after completion.

chunk_findings.detail: The fold never keeps review_id, combined_gates, or bursts, so a merged review is flattened. Evidence `{"review_id":"rev-9","combined_gates":["ci","unit_tests"],"note":"merged","round":2,"tree_sha":"abc","elapsed_s":10}` becomes a step with only gate/kind/step/elapsed_s/round/tree_sha; the merge note and peer identity are dropped, and overlapping process windows are reduced to a single `process_union_s` with no burst grouping.

chunk_findings.detail: `build` stores both next calls, but the rendered message prints only the CLI form. For any completed log, `text()` ends with `next: ddflow metrics paths` and never names `ddflow_metrics view=paths`.

chunk_findings.detail: A verdict that records the key with a JSON null, `{"combined_gates": null, "review_id": "rev-9", "gate": "ci"}`, makes `evidence.get("combined_gates", ())` return None rather than the default. The generator then iterates None and raises TypeError, so the whole facts fold aborts instead of treating a missing merge list as empty the way `review_id` and `tree_sha` already coerce null with `or ""`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/facts.py:combined_gates

chunk_findings.detail: The earlier merge-flattening defect is only partly fixed. `review_id` and `combined_gates` are copied, but a merged gate's note is still discarded: an outcome `note="merged"` (with `review_id="rev-9"`, `combined_gates=["ci","unit_tests"]`) becomes a step whose keys are only `at`, `gate`, `kind`, `step`, `elapsed_s`, `round`, `tree_sha`, `review_id`, `combined_gates`. The probe that checks those two fields does not put `note` on the step, so the merge explanation required by this change is still gone.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/metrics/paths.py:_steps

chunk_findings.detail: `_bursts` treats windows as closed (`start <= bursts[-1]["end"]`) while `_union_s` is half-open `[start, end)`. Windows `(0.0, 5.0)` and `(5.0, 8.0)` do not overlap, and `process_union_s` is 8 with no double-count, but `_bursts` merges them into one burst `{start: 0, end: 8, runs: 2, seconds: 8}`. Adjacent non-concurrent gates are reported as one concurrent burst.
